title: Rate-cap graceful degradation and metering offsets for non-chat tool executions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Customers execute multi-stage non-chat pipelines that combine embeddings generation, a rerank stage, and optional function/tool invocations that produce structured outputs. We currently overcharge or under-refund in scenarios where downstream tool executions partially fail, are rate-limited mid-flight, or are deduplicated by the runtime cache. This manifests as customer tickets, surprise invoices, and increased support load.

Problem statement: We need a deterministic, low-latency metering model for non-chat pipelines that: (1) enforces per-tenant rate caps gracefully (allowing in-flight requests to finish where possible), (2) attributes token/compute cost across pipeline stages with clear provenance, and (3) issues automated offsets/refunds when a downstream stage is not executed (partial failures, short-circuits, or runtime throttles). The model must be compatible with caching, batching, and speculative execution that the serving runtime performs.

Constraints: Must not add >2% p50 latency overhead for typical embedding+ranks+tool call path. Metering decisions should be replayable for offline reconciliation. Integration surface limited to hosted and Dedicated for this milestone (Private TBD).
proposed_solution:
High-level approach:
1) Two-phase provisional ledger entries: create a lightweight provisional charge at request acceptance that records candidate cost buckets (embedding, rerank, tool-exec). This provisional entry is non-billable until finalization.
2) Streaming provenance header: attach a short provenance token to the request containing stable request UUID and stage hints (e.g., stages=[embed,rerank,toolX]). This token flows through runtime components and is logged at finalization or abort.
3) Finalization and commit/offset protocol: when a request reaches terminal state (succeeded, failed, rate-limited, deduped), the runtime issues a finalize event. If a stage was not executed, we commit offsets that zero out the provisional entry for that stage. Offsets are idempotent and reference the original provisional ID.
4) Rate-cap grace window: when tenant rate cap is reached, allow an acceptance window of N=200ms (configurable) for in-flight requests to finish before rejecting new requests. Requests accepted past token issuance still get provisional entries but are marked for elevated review and potential offset if rejected.
5) Cache/batching compatibility: dedupe events from the cache will emit a cache-hit finalize that marks the tool-stage as skipped with a zero-offset delta to avoid double-billing. Batching will aggregate provisional entries and finalization will split commit deltas proportionally based on observed per-subrequest execution metadata.
6) Offline reconciliation: produce a daily reconciliation report comparing provisional -> committed state and highlight non-zero discrepancies for manual review and automated corrective jobs.

Implementation notes: store provisional entries in billing-queue (fast KV) for 48 hours to allow for delayed finalization; finalize events are durable and appended to billing ledger (immutable). Use request UUID + provisional ID as idempotency key. Add new metric streams for provisional_count, finalize_latency, offsets_issued_count.
acceptance_criteria:
- Provisional entries are created for 100% of non-chat embedding+ranks+toolcall requests in the staging cluster.
- Finalize events are emitted for >= 99.5% of requests within 10s of terminal state.
- Offsets are applied automatically for the following scenarios: downstream tool not executed, request deduplicated via cache, request rejected by rate-cap.
- End-to-end integration test that simulates 1000 mixed pipelines (50% tool success, 30% tool partial failure, 20% cache hits) shows net billing matches expected ledger within 0.1%.
- p50 latency overhead for metering adds <= 2% to baseline in the benchmark harness.
- Feature flag gate exists to rollback at runtime.
testing_plan:
Unit tests: provenance token creation, provisional entry lifecycle, idempotent finalize/offset operations.
Integration tests: local runtime harness that simulates batching + cache + tool endpoints with controllable failures. Run matrix for N=1000 requests across different sequence lengths and confirm ledger final state.
Load test: replay 10k/sec mixed traffic in staging for 1 hour; monitor finalize latency and provisional queue saturation.
Reconciliation: run daily job in staging against synthetic traffic seeded with known failures; ensure automated corrections do not exceed thresholds.
Manual QA: billing team to run smoke check against seed accounts with known quotas.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flagged rollout in staging for embed+ranks+non-chat tool pipelines. 2) Canary to 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours; monitor finalize rates, offsets issued, and customer-impacting errors. 3) Expand to 25% for 72 hours. 4) Full rollout to hosted + selected Dedicated tenants after sign-off.
Rollback: Use feature flag to disable provisional entries and revert to previous metering; reconciliation job will reconcile any provisional entries left.
metrics:
- billing.provisional.count (per-tenant)
- billing.finalize.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
- billing.offsets.count and billing.offsets.amount_usd
- billing.discrepancy.rate (provisional != committed)
- runtime.accept_window.expired_count
- customer_support.invoices.disputes_per_100k_requests
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Provisional queue growth during high load could cause memory pressure. Mitigation: set hard TTL (48h) and backpressure the acceptance path with rate-limited provisional writes; fail open to provisional but tag requests for offline audit if KV is saturated.
Risk: Incorrect splitting of aggregated batch finalizations may misattribute cost. Mitigation: include per-subrequest metadata (token counts, sequence length) in batch finalize and use deterministic proportional split. Add reconciliation alerts for >0.2% split variance.
Risk: Customers see temporary overcharges until offsets are applied. Mitigation: surface provisional state in Console (billing view) with clear labeling and same-day automated offsets where applicable. Prioritize high-visibility tenants for manual review.
